item.title: Elizabeth Holmes & Theranos | 60 Minutes Archive
item.description: Elizabeth Holmes claimed her start-up, Theranos, would revolutionizing blood testing, taking a pin-prick of blood and performing hundreds of laboratory tests. But as Norah O'Donnell reported in 2018, Theranos' machine never delivered on its promise, and Holmes is currently serving an 11-year prison sentence for defrauding investors.

item.title: Kristi Noem no longer serving as Trump envoy to Shield of the Americas
item.description: Former DHS Secretary Kristi Noem is no longer serving as the Trump administration's envoy to the Shield of the Americas initiative, a State Department official said. She is still at the department.

item.title: Feds probing suspicious letters to election officials, lawmakers
item.description: Federal investigators said they are looking into suspicious letters containing unknown substances that were mailed to state election officials and congressional offices.

item.title: Strait of Hormuz still unsafe for ships, maritime group warns
item.description: Vessels in the Strait of Hormuz still face "indiscriminate attacks" even if they switch off tracking systems, a maritime risk firm warns.

item.title: Late owner of Philadelphia's "house of horrors" was "the devil in disguise," woman says
item.description: Investigators are back at the so-called "house of horrors" in Philadelphia's Olney neighborhood after finding evidence of human DNA while using luminol in the home. CBS News correspondent Tom Hanson has the latest.

item.title: Exclusive video shows Cornell University Faculty Senate meeting
item.description: Exclusive video offers insight into Wednesday's high-stakes meeting at Cornell University.

item.title: White House's Katie Zacharia confirms she never passed bar exam
item.description: The White House described Katie Zacharia as "uniquely qualified" to be the new press secretary.

item.title: Ousted general warned of missile defense shortage before Iran war
item.description: Army Chief of Staff Gen. Randy George, later ousted by Defense Secretary Hegseth, said the shortage of missile defense munitions would extend into 2030.

item.title: Judge finds Musk, Noem targeted ex-FEMA official
item.description: A federal magistrate judge said Elon Musk and former Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem knowingly spread false information about Mary Comans, the former CFO of FEMA.

item.title: White House prepares plans to use "mother of all bombs" on Iran
item.description: The White House and Pentagon have prepared plans to use a Massive Ordnance Air Blast bomb to hit military sites in Iran if ordered by President Trump, sources familiar with the matter told CBS News.

item.title: Houthis building advanced missile system using Chinese parts, Wall Street Journal reports
item.description: The Houthis are attempting to produce their own ballistic missiles using Chinese parts, according to a new report from the Wall Street Journal. Aaron MacLean, host of "The School of War" podcast, joins CBS News to discuss.

item.title: Justice Department sues California over noncitizens getting ballots
item.description: The Justice Department sued California, alleging that the federal government has identified more than 20,000 noncitizens who are unlawfully registered to vote.

item.title: More workers are skipping doctor's visits over money worries
item.description: Roughly a third of employees said they put off or skipped medical or dental care in the past year because of financial concerns, a new survey found.

item.title: Eric Deters files defamation lawsuit against Kimberly Guilfoyle
item.description: Eric Deters, a GOP donor who said Kimberly Guilfoyle asked him to wire her $100,000, has sued her and her lawyers.

item.title: 9 fired FBI employees who worked on Trump documents case sue
item.description: Nine former FBI employees sued the bureau, saying they were unlawfully terminated for working on the investigation into President Trump's classified documents case.

item.title: ASU parts ways with hockey coach following player collapse
item.description: Matthew Mayich, a 21-year-old sophomore, collapsed during an Aug. 20 workout and had to be put on life support.

item.title: Winter may bring snow and rain to some drought-stricken U.S. states
item.description: NOAA's new winter weather outlook predicts wetter-than-usual conditions in some states plagued by long-standing drought.

item.title: As Jolly runs for Florida gov., he confronts prior ties to alleged fraudster
item.description: Shortly after David Jolly launched his campaign for Florida governor, his former boss was indicted for taking over $100 million from a disability nonprofit. Jolly says he wasn't aware of the scheme.

item.title: A massive Russian attack hit Kyiv. Ukraine claims the U.S. could have prevented it.
item.description: Ukraine says it is resuming strikes on Russian energy infrastructure after what it calls a betrayal on the part of the U.S. and SpaceX. American intelligence responded that it didn't warn Ukraine of an incoming Russian strike due to bad weather, sources say. CBS News' Aidan Stretch explains more.

item.title: Trump calls off plan to livestream Fort Hood shooter's execution
item.description: "He will die, as scheduled, by firing squad, but this event will not be streamed," President Trump wrote on Truth Social.

item.title: Venezuela's Maduro due in NYC court over conspiracy to commit torture charges
item.description: Former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, are slated to return to a U.S. court amid a new torture indictment. CBS News' Katrina Kaufman reports.

item.title: Cornell Greek life should end if found unsafe, school president says
item.description: Cornell University's Faculty Senate met on Wednesday to debate a resolution of no confidence in the school administration.

item.title: Americans are taking trips to Mexico for cosmetic treatments, even as potential risks remain
item.description: CBS California Investigates accompanied a group of women traveling from San Diego to Lipo Tijuana VIP, a medical spa that attracts patients from across the United States.

item.title: Pope Leo resumes some papal duties after surgery, Vatican says
item.description: Pope Leo XIV has resumed some work, the Vatican said Thursday, after he had a piece of his right lung removed and received a diagnosis of lung cancer.

item.title: Trump invokes executive privilege in Kennedy Center legal fight
item.description: President Trump has formally invoked executive privilege to shield certain records from a Democratic congresswoman who sits on the Kennedy Center board.

item.title: Amazon launches new AI devices that can listen and take notes
item.description: The products include a silicone wristband that can be clipped to clothing and a device that magnetically attaches to the back of a phone.

item.title: FTC issues subpoenas to Anthropic and OpenAI over safety incidents
item.description: The demands come amid mounting public concerns about the potential risks posed by frontier AI models.

item.title: Why AI could end the price tag as we know it
item.description: Retailers want to harness the power of artificial intelligence to set personalized prices for shoppers, a consumer protection expert says.

item.title: Ukraine reports U.S. early warning system shut down as Russia launched new air strikes
item.description: Ukrainian officials tell CBS News that a U.S. early warning system failed amid a new wave of Russian strikes on Tuesday. CBS News' Charlie D'Agata has the details.

item.title: About Us
item.description: "60 Minutes" airs Sundays at 7 p.m. ET/PT
